overclaims: In a July–August 2026 survey of 637 US and UK researchers, respondents reported average time savings of almost seven hours weekly across scientific work [e1].
These are self-reported gains, corroborated by the study’s broader evidence of scientific AI use.
checks.note: The source says about three quarters of researchers report time savings, averaging almost 7 hours. The rationale and e1 explanation instead credit that average to all respondents. The quoted e1 text does not show the 637 sample, the US/UK scope, the July–August 2026 timing or 'across scientific work', and the event_date 2026-08 can't be verified. The e1 explanation says usage data 'corroborates' the gains, but the contract excludes adoption alone, and e3 says the results show associations, not causality.
